title: Adaptive deviation denoiser and staged notifier for usage/cost/latency signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We get a high volume of noisy alerts from usage/cost/latency pipelines — many are transient bursts or telemetry artifacts that cause paging churn and obscure real regressions. Existing detectors are per-metric threshold/percentile rules and struggle with multi-tenant seasonality and correlated bursts. Goal: Build a noise-resistant detection & staged-notification system that reduces false positives (target >50% reduction in noisy pages) while keeping high recall for impactful incidents. Approach: hybrid pipeline that 1) computes tenant-aware baselines with robust denoising (median/quantile smoothing, seasonal decomposition), 2) runs a short-window ML scoring model to down-weight telemetry glitches, and 3) emits graded signals which the notification throttler converts into progressive notifications (silent console event -> low-severity email -> pager) with escalation windows and skip conditions. The system must support per-customer sensitivity, be backfillable for retroactive tuning, and expose explainability info in the Console incident card.
acceptance_criteria: New detector runs alongside existing pipeline (shadow mode) for 2 weeks with no alerting changes
False positive rate in shadow decreases by >=50% on historical spike dataset (billing & latency streams)
Console shows signal explanation: baseline, z-score, ML score, contributing dimensions
Notification throttler implements staged flow: console-only -> digest -> email -> pager
Runbook links and investigation links included in all pager notifications
Performance: detector adds <15% CPU load to aggregator workers and stays under 200ms per evaluation on 95th percentile

notes: Key trade-offs considered: (1) Pure rules vs ML — chose hybrid to keep predictable behavior and improve over time; (2) Per-tenant baselines vs global baselines — will compute both and allow override; (3) Notification UX: progressive staged model to avoid immediate paging on low-confidence signals. Plan to run backfill to validate against last 18 months. Ops: ensure throttler state is durable and transparent for postmortems.
